I know a guy, also a scientist,
he’s got three grades of schooling,
431:
and he can draw a ten-ruble note in half an hour—
you can’t tell it from real!
432:
- Well, is it him?
- Hell if I know... I’ll check.
433:
- Excuse me, do you have a match?
- I don’t smoke.
434:
- What? - No, not him.
- A cop. - Definitely.
435:
The check showed that at the addresses
of Docent’s accomplices, the helmet isn’t there.
436:
The last version remains—the cloakroom attendant
Prokhorov.
437:
However, we couldn’t check this version:
Prokhorov didn’t show up for the meeting.
438:
He likely suspected something. Quit his job,
didn’t come home.
440:
And to you, our deepest apologies, thank you very much.
Take off the wig, wash off the tattoos,
441:
go home, celebrate New Year’s. Thank you very much.
- And mine?
442:
And your wards—we’ll return them
to their place today.
443:
And if the cloakroom attendant turns up,
we might need you again?
444:
I didn’t want to tell you, but today
Bely—Docent—escaped from the colony.
445:
Unbelievable but true. It’s dangerous for you to stay
like this.
446:
Maybe tomorrow? It’s New Year’s after all, and they
also tried in their own way.
447:
We live outside the city, it’s unlikely
Docent can find us.
448:
Fine, but don’t take a step from the dacha!
Yes, we forwarded your letter
449:
to Sheremetyev’s wife, here’s her reply.
Addressed to him.
450:
- On the first you’ll have lunch with us, promise?
- We promise!
451:
Such a pity, such a good woman, and her father—
a fence, a speculator.
452:
Why are you yelling? Who allowed you out?
- He showed up... Not-so-good person.
454:
New Year has come. I wish that in this
new year, everything for you would be new.
455:
Anything can happen, but know this:
Wherever you are, wherever I am,
456:
I will always remember you,
I will definitely find you.
457:
- And now... one moment...
- Where’d he go?
458:
Who knows? You can’t make anything out
of him now.
459:
What’s there to make out? He says he’ll find us
wherever we are, and slit our throats.
461:
They say he nicked Ryaboy’s throat with a razor—snip, and goodbye.
- Gone completely savage, the jackal.
462:
Who came to you? Santa Claus came to you,
he brought you gifts!
463:
- Fedya, come here. - What did I do?
- Come on, come on. Wear them in good health, house slippers.
464:
- What the hell do I need them for? I don’t even have a home.
- You will, it’s all ahead.
465:
- For now they’ll come in handy in prison too. Wear them.
- All you do is croak.
466:
This is for you, Vasya... Gavrila Petrovich, this is for you.
- Thank you.
467:
- Pure wool.
- This is for you too.
470:
- Do you have to get drunk like a pig?
- What else is there to do?
471: We could just sit, talk heart to heart.
472:
I’m not a prosecutor to be talking heart to heart with you.
- We could play a game.
473:
Look at that! Found someone to play with you!
You’ve got nine aces in the deck.
474: Why does it have to be cards?
475:
Here’s a good game—cities.
I say “Moscow,”
476:
and you, to the last letter “A”—Astrakhan.
And you, to “N”—Novgorod, got it?
477: Now you, Fedya, say one starting with “D.”
478:
Vorkuta.
Why? I did time there.
479:
- Good. And you, then, with “A.”
- Jambul. - What’s Jambul got to do with it?
480:
Because it’s warm there, that’s my home,
that’s my mom.
481:
Then let’s play like this. I’ll go out, you’ll
hide something, I’ll come back—I’ll find it.
482:
- You’d better find our helmet.
- Shut up.
483:
- We’ll hide it and he’ll peek through a hole?
- Why? You go out and hide it.
484:
And you watch so I don’t peek.
Why me? Anything happens—right away Fedya.
485:
- I’ll rip your trap, you lousy bastard!
- Trap, trap...
486:
- Docent, were you ever little?
- I was.
487:
- You had a dad and mom?
- I did.
488: Why are you so mean? Why like a dog?
490:
- Came on your own.
- Ah, you’re here too.
491:
I was about to come to you, but I can feel it—
there’s an ambush there.
492: Mityai, I need a place to hide.
495:
- Excuse me, doctor, sorry to trouble you for nothing.
- It’s fine.
496:
Give him some valerian, warm tea, and let him sleep.
- Thank you.
497:
- Does it hurt, Garik?
- It hurts, Vasya. Read.
499:
“Hello dear Daddy! We found out
you’re in prison
500:
and we were very happy, because we thought
you were dead.”
501:
What bastard snitched to that little Khmyr
about Khmyr?
502:
“And Mom was happy too, because
when the letter came, she cried
503:
all day, and before that she said
you were a test pilot.”
505:
“And I’m happy anyway that you’re alive, because
Mom says
507:
Exactly! Weak-willed—lifted the shared money
and blamed it on the cabbie.
508: Skedaddle out of here! I’ll knock your horns off, you radish!
510:
Aren’t you ashamed! You’re 40 years old,
half your life is already lived.
511:
What’s behind you? What’s in the present?
What’s ahead?
512:
Darkness, filth, and nothing human!
Come to your senses before it’s too late. That’s my advice.
513:
Listen, Docent, we’ve got to scram:
the lady doctor will snitch to the police.
514:
- She won’t. - Why?
- I did her in—razor to the throat...
515: she’s in the well, you can take a look.
516: How much did I have? One year.
518:
How much for the kindergarten and the apartment?
Let’s say ten!
520:
And for a lousy 14 years I’m supposed to put up with
that viper?
521:
The one that put the old woman in the well?
Do what you want, I’m going to the police.
523:
And you? You’ll keep putting up with him
till death, will you?
524: Vas, I told him earlier: I have a runny nose, and he...
525:
Enough, I’m sick of your runny nose.
Come here...
526:
- Where are you here?
- Right here.
527:
- What are you up to?
- We’re going to clean the rug.
528:
Listen, comrades. Finita la commedia.
First of all, I’m taking this off.
530:
I’ll do my time and that’s it. I’ll quit!
Get a job.
531:
- As what? A guard at my native collective farm.
- Why a guard?
532:
I can clear snow, lay bricks, or be
a translator—I know English.
533:
If only we’d brought the hat too!
Who is Docent? A crook.
534:
- There are lots of crooks, but one hat.
- If we brought the helmet, they’d cut our time.
535: Where’d he put it? We’ve checked everywhere.
536:
Crook! Did I tell you I have a runny nose?
And you: Trap, trap.
537:
- Made me dive in weather like that!
- When did he make you dive?
538:
When they nabbed us. Remember? He says,
I’m fishing, and you dive.
539:
- Wait, what did he say about fishing then?
- That I was fishing in an ice hole,
540:
- and he says, Cross-Eyed, can you swim?
- He hid the helmet in the ice hole—that’s what!
541:
Right! I remember, not-so-good person!
In the ice hole—in Malakhovka!
542:
Why didn’t you say so? Jerk! You could’ve left a note when you hanged yourself.
- Let’s go.
543:
- And him?
- Forget it, let them pick him up themselves. Carrying a hog like that. Let’s go!
545:
- There’s nothing there.
- It’s there, on the bottom. Need to dive.
546:
Why me? Anything happens—right away Cross-Eyed.
Vas, tell him to go in himself.
547: I can’t! It’s cold, I’ll get sick.
548:
- Just now he was hanging himself, now he’s afraid of catching cold!
- Fitness greetings!
550:
- Where’s the boat station?
- Over there.
551: I’d finish you off, but I don’t have time to mess with you!
552:
Now it’s become two pieces.
And there’s another one at the dacha.
554:
- One!
- Well done, Fyodor Petrovich, well done!
555:
- Two.
- The more we turn in, the better.
